outputs: Confidence scores for knowledge boundary perception
Confidence scores for knowledge boundary perception
The models generate answers to open-domain questions, including free-form and multiple-choice formats, with and without Chain-of-Thought reasoning.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated tasks to 'Other:Question Answering' since all experiments are QA-based. Normalized dataset names and simplified output descriptions while adding confidence scoring as a key output.
Normalized metric names to consistent capitalization and removed duplicates. All metrics are used to evaluate the quality of confidence estimation for QA outputs.

methods: semantic consistency checking using an LLM

changes_made.explanation: Added explicit criteria and normalized method description. The paper uses Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct to evaluate semantic consistency between generated responses as part of baseline comparison.
No human evaluation was conducted in this paper - all evaluations are automated using metrics and LLM-based assessment.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on NLG evaluation through confidence estimation for question answering tasks. The extraction was generally accurate but needed some consolidation and normalization. The paper uses both traditional metrics (accuracy) and specialized confidence evaluation metrics (alignment, overconfidence, etc.). LLM-as-judge is used for baseline comparison but not as the primary evaluation method.
